meta.title: dataclass: Type of "<parameter>" could not be determined because it refers to itself
meta.fix_ref: none named (maintainer: 'This will be addressed in the next release'; fixed in 1.1.358 per the candidate mapping)
meta.build_notes: npm pyright@1.1.357 (2024-04-03) and pyright@1.1.358 (2024-04-10), as mapped by the candidate list; the reporter used 1.1.354.
meta.notes: The maintainer's analysis: evaluating dir_b first (for example on a hover) needs the dataclass's synthesized __init__, which needs the types of dir_a and dir_b: a circularity that depends on the evaluation order. Race pattern as in pyright-2983: an edit, a hover on dir_b before the server re-analyses, then compare after settling.

settings_note: The issue names no settings (pyright CLI and Pylance defaults); the session defaults apply.

files.source: issue body, first python code block (the class), preceded by the two import lines of the maintainer's comment
files.note: the issue's first code block has no imports; 'from dataclasses import dataclass' and 'from pathlib import Path' are taken from the maintainer's code block in the same issue

repro.steps: Open main.py and let the server analyze it. Edit the file (press Enter at the end) and hover the dir_a reference in dir_b's initializer ('dir_a.joinpath(...)') right away, before the server re-analyzes it; the maintainer explains the error appears when dir_b's value is evaluated first, which needs dir_a, which needs the dataclass's synthesized __init__, which needs dir_a and dir_b. Reported (intermittent): 'Type of ... could not be determined because it refers to itself'. After the server settles, the diagnostics of main.py and the hovers on dir_a and dir_b must equal those of a fresh session on the same final text.

attempts.summary: Edit, then an immediate hover on the declared name dir_b (line 8, character 4), then compare diagnostics and hovers with a fresh session: equal on both builds (0/3). A hover on the declared name shows the declared type Path and does not evaluate the initializer, so it does not start the evaluation chain the maintainer describes.
